items.description: Review request R7922bcafda1e (8/5 RPR identification discrepancy). The 2026-08-05 quantitative RPR (Ra1100072bf01, Nonreactive) filed in this episode's chart is linked to specimen Rd7a8a161a61b, whose collection label reads GREENE, WALTER / MRN 74158126 / DOB 1960-11-18 (matching this patient), while the laboratory accessioning entry for the same accession A2608-2838 (Basic R8afce1668a21) reads NGUYEN, THAO / MRN 40718826 / DOB 1990-03-02. Under the local convention a specimen and its result belong to the patient identified by MRN and DOB on both the collection record and the accessioning entry; because these identify different patients the specimen's patient is unresolved, so whether this result belongs to a different patient cannot be determined. No later signed correction by either record's author resolves the discrepancy, so the conflict is unresolved.

Late latent syphilis (Condition R0fa2dc5c6733); first benzathine penicillin dose 2024-08-12 (R2d42efddbddc). CDC 2021 recommends nontreponemal titers at 6, 12 and 24 months after treatment of latent syphilis. The 6-month test (due 2025-02-12, collected 2025-02-20, R70fefa59a83b) and the 12-month test (due 2025-08-12, collected 2025-08-14, R8511d5cd4d56) were both in window. The 24-month test was due 2026-08-12, window 2026-07-13 to 2026-09-11, which closed before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. The only candidate collection in that window is specimen Rd7a8a161a61b / result Ra1100072bf01 of 2026-08-05, whose collection label (GREENE, WALTER, MRN 74158126, DOB 1960-11-18) and accessioning entry (Basic R8afce1668a21: NGUYEN, THAO, MRN 40718826, DOB 1990-03-02) identify different patients, so the specimen's patient is unresolved. Whether a specimen from this patient was collected in the window therefore depends on an unresolved source conflict.

Secondary syphilis diagnosed 2025-11-04 (walk-in note R8c7e65f32e85: diffuse maculopapular rash of trunk, palms and soles, oral ulcer, RPR 1:64 reactive Rc1e01001897e, treponemal test reactive), more than 30 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. The only therapy given was azithromycin 2 g PO (R7649bfea645b). CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 recommend benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose for primary, secondary and early latent syphilis; azithromycin is not a recommended or alternative regimen for syphilis because of documented macrolide resistance in T. pallidum. Doxycycline 100 mg BID for 14 days would have been the acceptable alternative for a non-pregnant patient who refuses injection. No penicillin or doxycycline was ever given (follow-up note R7913a7ec16f8 documents continued refusal of injection and no alternative oral regimen), and the RPR remains reactive at 1:16 on 2026-05-12 (R63e65d051478). The patient is male and not pregnant. Treatment is inadequate for the infection.

Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-07-13 (Condition Ra97bed23c0ae; RPR 1:2 reactive, Radad9c2d8475), 73 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses (7.2 million units total) for late latent syphilis, and this is the regimen for pregnant as well as non-pregnant patients. Only dose 1 of 3 was given, on 2026-07-13 (Rab78b047578c, noted 'R gluteal. 1/3.'). Doses 2 and 3 were missed (no-shows 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-27, Rf9db26ead311 and R39055295d8e0) and the 2026-09-15 visit note (R650558441f29) states the series will be restarted once an hCG returns; no further doses are recorded. Treatment is inadequate on either pregnancy status.

Treatment for this late latent episode is incomplete (only 1 of 3 benzathine penicillin doses, Rab78b047578c), so if the patient was pregnant at any time from the 2026-07-13 diagnosis to the evaluation time the pregnancy issue would exist. Serum hCG was negative at diagnosis (R8cfaea610acb, 2026-07-13), but on 2026-09-15 she reported an LMP about 7 weeks earlier and a serum quantitative hCG was collected (R650558441f29). That specimen was collected before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time and has no final result: Observation R5dd8ded81561 is status registered with the laboratory comment 'In process.' Whether she was pregnant during the episode therefore turns on a pending test result.

Early latent syphilis (Condition R76b8fbdf9e4c) treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-07-07 (Rfaf358a1eb02). CDC 2021 recommends nontreponemal titers at 6, 12 and 24 months. The 6-month test was in window (due 2026-01-07, collected 2026-01-15, R08756c9095fb). The 12-month test was due 2026-07-07 with a window of 2026-06-07 to 2026-08-06, which closed before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time, and no specimen from this patient was collected in that window at this clinic. The 2026-08-12 outreach note (Ra01873897ab4) records the patient stating she had 'the syphilis blood test' in July at her PCP, Dr. Lin at Maple Family Medicine, and that a request was faxed for the result. Under the local convention care at another facility is established only by a record from that facility received by the clinic, and no Maple Family Medicine record has been received, so whether a qualifying specimen was collected within the window cannot be determined.

Review request Rda4d87e0618a (third Bicillin dose 14 days after the second). Latent syphilis of unknown duration / late latent, diagnosed 2025-03-03 (Condition Rf59677b93814) in a patient who was pregnant at 18w3d that day (R2766ce143e8a). Doses were given 2025-03-03 (R94823194117b) and 2025-03-10 (R3730cec6d469); the third-week dose was missed for lack of transport (Rb9ddc85d5728) and given 2025-03-24 (R0678354279b3), 14 days after the second (R960530488cb5 confirms it was 'a week late'). CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 state that while an interval of 10-14 days between doses might be acceptable for non-pregnant patients, missed doses are not acceptable for pregnant patients receiving therapy for latent syphilis, and a pregnant patient who misses any dose must repeat the entire course. Given this patient's pregnancy status the interrupted series was not adequate therapy and no repeat course was given, so the issue is confirmed.

The patient was pregnant from before the 2025-03-03 diagnosis (18w3d, R2766ce143e8a) until delivery on 2025-08-01 (Riverside Hospital L&D discharge summary R362516686c03, a record from that facility received by the clinic). Treatment for latent syphilis of unknown duration in pregnancy requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses with no missed doses; CDC 2021 states that pregnant patients who miss any dose of therapy must repeat the full course. The third dose was given 2025-03-24, 14 days after the 2025-03-10 dose, because the 2025-03-17 dose was missed (Rb9ddc85d5728), and the course was never repeated. Treatment began 2025-03-03, which is more than 30 days before the 2025-08-01 delivery, so the timing requirement is met, but the regimen itself was not adequate for syphilis in pregnancy.

The 2026-06-16 quantitative RPR (Observation R29b26b182ad8, Nonreactive) is filed with this patient as subject, but its specimen collection record (Specimen R4c90adf34f8e, accession A2606-2157) carries label name ORTIZ, SAMANTHA with MRN 48305482 and DOB 1998-08-13, and the laboratory accessioning entry for the same accession (Basic R1e96d0922c32) also reads ORTIZ, SAMANTHA / 48305482 / 1998-08-13. Samuel Ortega is MRN 24530063, DOB 1983-01-26. Because the collection record and the accessioning entry agree and both identify Samantha Ortiz (Patient P86f7f3d), the specimen and its result belong to her, not to this patient. A laboratory result belonging to a different patient is filed in this episode's chart.

Primary syphilis (Condition Rb77ea6daec4d) treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-06-09 (R77d6d14a53db). CDC 2021 recommends nontreponemal titers at 6 and 12 months after treatment of primary syphilis. The 6-month test was in window (due 2025-12-09, collected 2025-12-11, Re0f8e2aef406). The 12-month test was due 2026-06-09 with a window of 2026-05-10 to 2026-07-09, which closed before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. The only RPR filed in this chart in that window, Observation R29b26b182ad8 of 2026-06-16, rests on specimen R4c90adf34f8e whose collection label and accessioning entry (Basic R1e96d0922c32) both identify Samantha Ortiz, MRN 48305482, DOB 1998-08-13, so it is not a specimen from this patient. No specimen from Samuel Ortega was collected in the window, and no outreach or outside record suggests otherwise, so the 12-month follow-up test was not collected within its window.

Primary syphilis diagnosed 2026-04-20 (Condition Re1cac7dd6145; indurated painless chancre, RPR 1:16 reactive Re4bdecc928e7, treponemal test reactive), more than 30 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose. The ordered injection was never given: MedicationAdministration Rab08552226b7 has status not-done with the note 'Pt left the clinic before the injection was given.' Outreach failed (R8f41005f28cc) and a DIS referral was placed for untreated primary syphilis (R7db676cad2c0). No other treatment of any kind is recorded, and the patient is male and not pregnant, so the episode remains untreated.

Review request R0db9ef904603 (only one of three Bicillin doses in our administration record). Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2025-04-14 (Condition Rde97ef6f5e9c) requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses. Dose 1 was given here on 2025-04-14 (R08ad4910274b). Because weekly travel was impossible, doses 2 and 3 were transferred to the County Health Department STD Clinic with a signed release (R3236bca81c51), and the clinic has received that facility's own faxed medication administration record (DocumentReference Rf4b6f607dc06, author County Health Department STD Clinic), documenting Bicillin L-A 2.4 MU IM on 2025-04-21 and 2025-04-28 and stating the series is complete 3 of 3. The outside care is therefore established by a record from that facility received by the clinic, and the three doses fall at 7-day intervals. Treatment is adequate for late latent syphilis in a non-pregnant male; the gap is only in the clinic's internal MAR.

Review request R9742468728aa (no 12-month RPR result in this chart). Early latent syphilis (Condition R312b4315e4e1) treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-06-23 (R358faf9cf732); titers are due at 6, 12 and 24 months. The 6-month test was in window (due 2025-12-23, collected 2025-12-29, R0279bed8a8ae). The 12-month test was due 2026-06-23, window 2026-05-24 to 2026-07-23. A specimen from this patient was collected on 2026-06-16 within that window: Specimen R4c90adf34f8e, label ORTIZ, SAMANTHA / MRN 48305482 / DOB 1998-08-13, matching this patient, and the laboratory accessioning entry for the same accession A2606-2157 (Basic R1e96d0922c32) carries the identical identifiers, so the specimen is hers. The nursing note of 2026-06-16 (R1f9eae76e46b) documents the 12-month draw. The specimen was not rejected and was resulted as Nonreactive; the result was simply filed in Samuel Ortega's chart (Observation R29b26b182ad8), which is a misfiling in that chart rather than a missed collection here. The test was collected within its window, so follow-up is not overdue.

Review request R798fc8df7ab4 (one Bicillin injection documented; is treatment complete). Syphilis diagnosed 2026-03-10, more than 30 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. The diagnostic note (R96a2514fb74d) records an asymptomatic new patient found on a pre-operative screen: RPR 1:16 (R0ead57315bb5) with reactive TP-PA (R42a74980be01), no sores, rash, alopecia, visual, hearing or neurologic findings, no known prior syphilis testing, and no documented negative test within the preceding year. With no evidence that infection was acquired within the past 12 months, this is latent syphilis of unknown duration, which CDC 2021 directs be treated as late latent: benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses. Only a single dose was given, on 2026-03-10 (R86fd16f52ecf, 1.2 MU in each ventrogluteal site for 2.4 MU total), and the 2026-03-24 call note (R9df69739138f) records that no further appointments were scheduled. Serum hCG was negative (R7d1db2470e17) and nothing indicates pregnancy, so the required regimen is three weekly doses. Two doses are missing; treatment is inadequate.

Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2025-06-02 (Condition R7a35247e4cfc) requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses. Doses were given 2025-06-02 (R28fb18460ef4) and 2025-06-09 (Radd0c0084f66), but the 2025-06-16 dose was cancelled for out-of-state travel (Rda877498a8cf) and the third dose was not given until 2025-06-27 (R49231f4025c9), 18 days after the second. CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 note that for non-pregnant patients an interval of 10-14 days between doses of benzathine penicillin might be acceptable before restarting the sequence of injections; an 18-day interval exceeds that allowance, so the sequence should have been restarted. No restarted course is recorded (R84aa6677a1c5 simply declares the series complete). The patient is male and not pregnant. Treatment as given is not adequate for late latent syphilis.

Review request R0d7a56e007e3 (specimen label name does not match the current chart name for the 4/8 RPR). The 2026-04-08 quantitative RPR (Observation Rc7f2214aaf95, Reactive 1:4) rests on specimen R2e18a9ea8714, whose label reads GOMEZ, MARIA with MRN 53229432 and DOB 1989-04-02, and the laboratory accessioning entry for the same accession A2604-6204 (Basic Re7b5f29d83cd) reads GOMEZ, MARIA / 53229432 / 1989-04-02. Under the local convention the specimen and its result belong to the patient identified by medical record number and date of birth on the collection record and on the accessioning entry; both carry this patient's MRN 53229432 and DOB 1989-04-02, and they agree with each other, so the specimen is hers. The name difference is explained by the registration update of 2026-01-12 (R2b6fca07ed75), which documents a legal name change from Maria Gomez to Maria Reyes with the MRN unchanged. The result does not belong to a different patient.

Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-06-15 (Condition R8a5c5740c37c; RPR 1:16 with a nonreactive RPR 2025-11-20) in a patient with documented penicillin anaphylaxis (AllergyIntolerance R9e3c58cd24c2). She was dispensed and completed doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 14 days (MedicationDispense R351b92b15d48, 28 capsules; completion with no missed doses confirmed 2026-07-02, Ra2529680b361). Under CDC 2021 that is an acceptable alternative regimen for early syphilis in a non-pregnant, penicillin-allergic patient, but doxycycline is contraindicated in pregnancy: pregnant patients with syphilis must be treated with penicillin, desensitized if necessary. Pregnancy status is not established. The 2026-06-15 note (R43ca69f3d617) records an uncertain LMP with irregular cycles, and the serum quantitative hCG collected that day before the evaluation time has no final result (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, 'Specimen forwarded to reference laboratory'). Because adequacy depends on the patient's pregnancy status, which turns on that pending result, the issue cannot be determined.

The only syphilis therapy for this episode is doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days (MedicationDispense R351b92b15d48, completed per Ra2529680b361), which is not adequate treatment for syphilis in pregnancy; CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G, with penicillin desensitization for pregnant patients reporting penicillin allergy such as this patient's documented anaphylaxis (R9e3c58cd24c2). So the issue exists if and only if she was pregnant at some time between the 2026-06-15 diagnosis and the evaluation time. That fact is not established: the diagnosis-day note records an uncertain LMP with irregular cycles (R43ca69f3d617) and the serum quantitative hCG collected 2026-06-15, before the evaluation time, still has no final result (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, specimen forwarded to a reference laboratory). No delivery or other pregnancy record exists. The issue depends on a pending test result.

Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-05-19 (Condition Rbc8a9536c239; RPR 1:32, Rd403a1b46258), more than 30 days before the evaluation time. Adequate therapy is benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose. The administration record states that 2.4 million units IM were given on 2026-05-19 (MedicationAdministration R4e79a3b01676, status completed), but the pharmacy records conflict: only one 1,200,000-unit prefilled syringe was dispensed for him (MedicationDispense Rd6c2676fca98, quantity 1) and the pharmacist's signed end-of-day reconciliation states that one 1.2 MU syringe was released for this patient and that no second syringe was pulled from clinic stock for him per the cabinet log (DocumentReference R41e1cb337160). If only 1.2 million units were administered the dose is half the required amount. The two accounts are by different authors, so there is no later signed correction by a record's author to govern, and no other convention settles it; the administered dose is therefore an unresolved source conflict and adequacy cannot be determined.

Review request Re4a6b729e9c5 (was maternal treatment adequate for this delivery). The patient was pregnant from the 2026-01-05 diagnosis, presenting at 35w1d with latent syphilis of unknown duration (Rabd804816606, Condition R35a03bed1367). She received the correct regimen, benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses, on 2026-01-05, 2026-01-12 and 2026-01-19 at exactly 7-day intervals (Rc541e07b1a97, R0083a427d4e3, Reb8ecf233de2; series completion confirmed at 38w1d, Reef7fc18efd3). However, once delivery has occurred that treatment must have begun at least 30 days before it, and treatment began 2026-01-05, so 2026-02-04 is the decisive date. The delivery date is not established: the only record of it is the 2026-02-20 telephone note in which the patient reports having delivered at Mercy General, with maternal delivery records and the newborn discharge summary requested from Mercy General (R2f4e5f4a8666). At 35w1d on 2026-01-05 her estimated due date was about 2026-02-08, so delivery could have fallen on either side of 2026-02-04. Care at another facility is established only by a record from that facility received by the clinic, and no Mercy General record has been received, so the issue cannot be determined.

Latent syphilis of unknown duration diagnosed 2025-09-15 (Condition Rb979a379e9e2; asymptomatic, last negative test unknown, RPR 1:8), more than 30 days before the evaluation time. CDC 2021 directs that latent syphilis of unknown duration be treated as late latent with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses, and the plan was documented as weekly x3 with return visits 9/22 and 9/29 (R9314a09ccd1b). Only the first dose was given, on 2025-09-15 (R302e2c011a98). The patient did not attend for doses 2 or 3 (no-shows documented 2025-09-22 and 2025-09-29 with voicemails and a mailed letter, R5bb174ddeeae and R7ce2618288da) and no further doses appear anywhere in the chart; the RPR remained reactive at 1:4 on 2026-03-20 (R289dfecbca57). CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose (or, for a non-pregnant penicillin-allergic patient, doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days). No treatment was given: the visit note (R9a3fac1743ab) records that Bicillin was withheld on the reasoning that intermittent doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis had 'likely already partially treated' him, with a plan only to recheck the RPR. The only doxycycline in the chart is doxy-PEP, 20 tablets taken as 200 mg once within 72 hours after condomless sex (MedicationDispense R3496d34508d3 and refill R805872901be8), which is not a syphilis treatment regimen and does not substitute for one. The RPR remained reactive at 1:16 on 2026-05-11 (R7d7a505d7a28). The patient is male and not pregnant. The episode is untreated.

Review request R79d6d8df8dd9 (12-month RPR has no result on file). Primary syphilis (Condition R8221b078a309) treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-08-18 (Rdbe347ecbfcf); CDC 2021 recommends nontreponemal titers at 6 and 12 months. The 6-month test was in window (due 2026-02-18, collected 2026-02-24, R302c2679dbee). The 12-month test was due 2026-08-18, window 2026-07-19 to 2026-09-17. A serum specimen from this patient was collected 2026-09-14, inside that window: Specimen Raaaa95a95502 with label SCOTT, BRIANNA / MRN 55961553 / DOB 2001-03-17, matching the accessioning entry for accession A2609-2197 (Basic R0e0e55d93c73) and this patient's identifiers. The laboratory did not reject it; the comment on Observation R1e1c26c47f5d (status registered) is 'Received at reference laboratory. Result to follow.' Under the local convention a test is collected within its window when a specimen from the patient was collected then and not rejected, which is satisfied here, so follow-up is not overdue. The missing result is a pending result, not a missed collection.

Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-01-20 (Condition R049a64ea2ca4) requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses. Only dose 1 of 3 is recorded here, on 2026-01-20 (MedicationAdministration R7190edc51f1a, 'R gluteal. #1 of 3.'). On 2026-01-29 the patient reported that she had moved to Riverton, had received her second Bicillin injection at Eastside Community Health on 2026-01-27, and had the third scheduled there for 2026-02-03; a release of information was signed and faxed (R496b28b30760), and a second request was faxed on 2026-03-02 with no response to the first (R5c674c520644). Under the local convention care at another facility is established only by a record from that facility received by the clinic, and no Eastside Community Health administration record has been received. Whether doses 2 and 3 were given, and so whether treatment is adequate, depends on that outstanding outside record. Serology is consistent with either possibility (RPR 1:1 on 2026-07-22, R53468b9b4173).

The two accounts are by different authors, so there is no later signed correction by a record's author to govern, and no other convention settles it; the administered dose is therefore an unresolved source conflict and adequacy cannot be determined.

Given this patient's pregnancy status the interrupted series was not adequate therapy and no repeat course was given, so the issue is confirmed.

The patient was pregnant from before the 2025-03-03 diagnosis (18w3d, R2766ce143e8a) until delivery on 2025-08-01 (Riverside Hospital L&D discharge summary R362516686c03, a record from that facility received by the clinic). The third dose was given 2025-03-24, 14 days after the 2025-03-10 dose, because the 2025-03-17 dose was missed (Rb9ddc85d5728), and the course was never repeated. Treatment began 2025-03-03, which is more than 30 days before the 2025-08-01 delivery, so the timing requirement is met, but the regimen itself was not adequate for syphilis in pregnancy.

CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 recommend benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose for primary, secondary and early latent syphilis; azithromycin is not a recommended or alternative regimen for syphilis because of documented macrolide resistance in T. pallidum. Doxycycline 100 mg BID for 14 days would have been the acceptable alternative for a non-pregnant patient who refuses injection. Whether she was pregnant during the episode therefore turns on a pending test result.

Review request Rda4d87e0618a (third Bicillin dose 14 days after the second). Latent syphilis of unknown duration / late latent, diagnosed 2025-03-03 (Condition Rf59677b93814) in a patient who was pregnant at 18w3d that day (R2766ce143e8a). Doses were given 2025-03-03 (R94823194117b) and 2025-03-10 (R3730cec6d469); the third-week dose was missed for lack of transport (Rb9ddc85d5728) and given 2025-03-24 (R0678354279b3), 14 days after the second (R960530488cb5 confirms it was 'a week late'). CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 state that while an interval of 10-14 days between doses might be acceptable for non-pregnant patients, missed doses are not acceptable for pregnant patients receiving therapy for latent syphilis, and a pregnant patient who misses any dose must repeat the entire course. Given this patient's pregnancy status the interrupted series was not adequate therapy and no repeat course was given, so the issue is confirmed.

The patient was pregnant from before the 2025-03-03 diagnosis (18w3d, R2766ce143e8a) until delivery on 2025-08-01 (Riverside Hospital L&D discharge summary R362516686c03, a record from that facility received by the clinic). Treatment for latent syphilis of unknown duration in pregnancy requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses with no missed doses; CDC 2021 states that pregnant patients who miss any dose of therapy must repeat the full course. The third dose was given 2025-03-24, 14 days after the 2025-03-10 dose, because the 2025-03-17 dose was missed (Rb9ddc85d5728), and the course was never repeated. Treatment began 2025-03-03, which is more than 30 days before the 2025-08-01 delivery, so the timing requirement is met, but the regimen itself was not adequate for syphilis in pregnancy.

No restarted course is recorded (R84aa6677a1c5 simply declares the series complete). The patient is male and not pregnant. Treatment as given is not adequate for late latent syphilis.

Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-06-15 (Condition R8a5c5740c37c; RPR 1:16 with a nonreactive RPR 2025-11-20) in a patient with documented penicillin anaphylaxis (AllergyIntolerance R9e3c58cd24c2). Pregnancy status is not established. The 2026-06-15 note (R43ca69f3d617) records an uncertain LMP with irregular cycles, and the serum quantitative hCG collected that day before the evaluation time has no final result (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, 'Specimen forwarded to reference laboratory'). The only syphilis therapy for this episode is doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days (MedicationDispense R351b92b15d48, completed per Ra2529680b361), which is not adequate treatment for syphilis in pregnancy; CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G, with penicillin desensitization for pregnant patients reporting penicillin allergy such as this patient's documented anaphylaxis (R9e3c58cd24c2). So the issue exists if and only if she was pregnant at some time between the 2026-06-15 diagnosis and the evaluation time. That fact is not established: the diagnosis-day note records an uncertain LMP with irregular cycles (R43ca69f3d617) and the serum quantitative hCG collected 2026-06-15, before the evaluation time, still has no final result (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, specimen forwarded to a reference laboratory). Review request Rda4d87e0618a (third Bicillin dose 14 days after the second). Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2025-06-02 (Condition R7a35247e4cfc) requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses. No restarted course is recorded (R84aa6677a1c5 simply declares the series complete). The patient is male and not pregnant. Treatment as given is not adequate for late latent syphilis.

Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-06-15 (Condition R8a5c5740c37c; RPR 1:16 with a nonreactive RPR 2025-11-20) in a patient with documented penicillin anaphylaxis (AllergyIntolerance R9e3c58cd24c2). Pregnancy status is not established. The 2026-06-15 note (R43ca69f3d617) records an uncertain LMP with irregular cycles, and the serum quantitative hCG collected that day before the evaluation time has no final result (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, 'Specimen forwarded to reference laboratory'). The only syphilis therapy for this episode is doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days (MedicationDispense R351b92b15d48, completed per Ra2529680b361), which is not adequate treatment for syphilis in pregnancy; CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G, with penicillin desensitization for pregnant patients reporting penicillin allergy such as this patient's documented anaphylaxis (R9e3c58cd24c2). So the issue exists if and only if she was pregnant at some time between the 2026-06-15 diagnosis and the evaluation time. That fact is not established: the diagnosis-day note records an uncertain LMP with irregular cycles (R43ca69f3d617) and the serum quantitative hCG collected 2026-06-15, before the evaluation time, still has no final result (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, specimen forwarded to a reference laboratory). No delivery or other pregnancy record exists. The issue depends on a pending test result.

Review request R9742468728aa (no 12-month RPR result in this chart). The nursing note of 2026-06-16 (R1f9eae76e46b) documents the 12-month draw. Early latent syphilis (Condition Ree07a4fa48b4) treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-02-24 (R76a7ae364846). CDC 2021 recommends nontreponemal titers at 6, 12 and 24 months. The 6-month test was in window (due 2025-08-24, collected 2025-09-02, Ra66fa8daaa9c). The 12-month test was due 2026-02-24 with a window of 2026-01-25 to 2026-03-26, which closed before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. Review request R798fc8df7ab4 (one Bicillin injection documented; is treatment complete). Syphilis diagnosed 2026-03-10, more than 30 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. The diagnostic note (R96a2514fb74d) records an asymptomatic new patient found on a pre-operative screen: RPR 1:16 (R0ead57315bb5) with reactive TP-PA (R42a74980be01), no sores, rash, alopecia, visual, hearing or neurologic findings, no known prior syphilis testing, and no documented negative test within the preceding year. With no evidence that infection was acquired within the past 12 months, this is latent syphilis of unknown duration, which CDC 2021 directs be treated as late latent: benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses. Only a single dose was given, on 2026-03-10 (R86fd16f52ecf, 1.2 MU in each ventrogluteal site for 2.4 MU total), and the 2026-03-24 call note (R9df69739138f) records that no further appointments were scheduled. Serum hCG was negative (R7d1db2470e17) and nothing indicates pregnancy, so the required regimen is three weekly doses. Two doses are missing; treatment is inadequate.

Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2025-06-02 (Condition R7a35247e4cfc) requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses. Doses were given 2025-06-02 (R28fb18460ef4) and 2025-06-09 (Radd0c0084f66), but the 2025-06-16 dose was cancelled for out-of-state travel (Rda877498a8cf) and the third dose was not given until 2025-06-27 (R49231f4025c9), 18 days after the second. CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 note that for non-pregnant patients an interval of 10-14 days between doses of benzathine penicillin might be acceptable before restarting the sequence of injections; an 18-day interval exceeds that allowance, so the sequence should have been restarted. No restarted course is recorded (R84aa6677a1c5 simply declares the series complete). The patient is male and not pregnant. Treatment as given is not adequate for late latent syphilis.

Review request R0d7a56e007e3 (specimen label name does not match the current chart name for the 4/8 RPR). The 2026-04-08 quantitative RPR (Observation Rc7f2214aaf95, Reactive 1:4) rests on specimen R2e18a9ea8714, whose label reads GOMEZ, MARIA with MRN 53229432 and DOB 1989-04-02, and the laboratory accessioning entry for the same accession A2604-6204 (Basic Re7b5f29d83cd) reads GOMEZ, MARIA / 53229432 / 1989-04-02. Under the local convention the specimen and its result belong to the patient identified by medical record number and date of birth on the collection record and on the accessioning entry; both carry this patient's MRN 53229432 and DOB 1989-04-02, and they agree with each other, so the specimen is hers. The name difference is explained by the registration update of 2026-01-12 (R2b6fca07ed75), which documents a legal name change from Maria Gomez to Maria Reyes with the MRN unchanged. The result does not belong to a different patient.

Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-06-15 (Condition R8a5c5740c37c; RPR 1:16 with a nonreactive RPR 2025-11-20) in a patient with documented penicillin anaphylaxis (AllergyIntolerance R9e3c58cd24c2). She was dispensed and completed doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 14 days (MedicationDispense R351b92b15d48, 28 capsules; completion with no missed doses confirmed 2026-07-02, Ra2529680b361). Under CDC 2021 that is an acceptable alternative regimen for early syphilis in a non-pregnant, penicillin-allergic patient, but doxycycline is contraindicated in pregnancy: pregnant patients with syphilis must be treated with penicillin, desensitized if necessary. Pregnancy status is not established. The 2026-06-15 note (R43ca69f3d617) records an uncertain LMP with irregular cycles, and the serum quantitative hCG collected that day before the evaluation time has no final result (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, 'Specimen forwarded to reference laboratory'). Because adequacy depends on the patient's pregnancy status, which turns on that pending result, the issue cannot be determined.

The only syphilis therapy for this episode is doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days (MedicationDispense R351b92b15d48, completed per Ra2529680b361), which is not adequate treatment for syphilis in pregnancy; CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G, with penicillin desensitization for pregnant patients reporting penicillin allergy such as this patient's documented anaphylaxis (R9e3c58cd24c2). So the issue exists if and only if she was pregnant at some time between the 2026-06-15 diagnosis and the evaluation time. That fact is not established: the diagnosis-day note records an uncertain LMP with irregular cycles (R43ca69f3d617) and the serum quantitative hCG collected 2026-06-15, before the evaluation time, still has no final result (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, specimen forwarded to a reference laboratory). No delivery or other pregnancy record exists. The issue depends on a pending test result.

Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-05-19 (Condition Rbc8a9536c239; RPR 1:32, Rd403a1b46258), more than 30 days before the evaluation time. Adequate therapy is benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose. The administration record states that 2.4 million units IM were given on 2026-05-19 (MedicationAdministration R4e79a3b01676, status completed), but the pharmacy records conflict: only one 1,200,000-unit prefilled syringe was dispensed for him (MedicationDispense Rd6c2676fca98, quantity 1) and the pharmacist's signed end-of-day reconciliation states that one 1.2 MU syringe was released for this patient and that no second syringe was pulled from clinic stock for him per the cabinet log (DocumentReference R41e1cb337160). If only 1.2 million units were administered the dose is half the required amount. The two accounts are by different authors, so there is no later signed correction by a record's author to govern, and no other convention settles it; the administered dose is therefore an unresolved source conflict and adequacy cannot be determined.

Review request Re4a6b729e9c5 (was maternal treatment adequate for this delivery). The patient was pregnant from the 2026-01-05 diagnosis, presenting at 35w1d with latent syphilis of unknown duration (Rabd804816606, Condition R35a03bed1367). She received the correct regimen, benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses, on 2026-01-05, 2026-01-12 and 2026-01-19 at exactly 7-day intervals (Rc541e07b1a97, R0083a427d4e3, Reb8ecf233de2; series completion confirmed at 38w1d, Reef7fc18efd3). However, once delivery has occurred that treatment must have begun at least 30 days before it, and treatment began 2026-01-05, so 2026-02-04 is the decisive date. The delivery date is not established: the only record of it is the 2026-02-20 telephone note in which the patient reports having delivered at Mercy General, with maternal delivery records and the newborn discharge summary requested from Mercy General (R2f4e5f4a8666). At 35w1d on 2026-01-05 her estimated due date was about 2026-02-08, so delivery could have fallen on either side of 2026-02-04. Care at another facility is established only by a record from that facility received by the clinic, and no Mercy General record has been received, so the issue cannot be determined.

Latent syphilis of unknown duration diagnosed 2025-09-15 (Condition Rb979a379e9e2; asymptomatic, last negative test unknown, RPR 1:8), more than 30 days before the evaluation time. CDC 2021 directs that latent syphilis of unknown duration be treated as late latent with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses, and the plan was documented as weekly x3 with return visits 9/22 and 9/29 (R9314a09ccd1b). Only the first dose was given, on 2025-09-15 (R302e2c011a98). The patient did not attend for doses 2 or 3 (no-shows documented 2025-09-22 and 2025-09-29 with voicemails and a mailed letter, R5bb174ddeeae and R7ce2618288da) and no further doses appear anywhere in the chart; the RPR remained reactive at 1:4 on 2026-03-20 (R289dfecbca57). The patient is male and not pregnant. Treatment is inadequate.

Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-02-09 (Condition R06e8453cba94; RPR 1:32 reactive, Ra86dbdfb653a, with a nonreactive RPR in 10/2025 and reactive TP-PA), more than 30 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. No treatment was given: the visit note (R9a3fac1743ab) records that Bicillin was withheld on the reasoning that intermittent doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis had 'likely already partially treated' him, with a plan only to recheck the RPR. The only doxycycline in the chart is doxy-PEP, 20 tablets taken as 200 mg once within 72 hours after condomless sex (MedicationDispense R3496d34508d3 and refill R805872901be8), which is not a syphilis treatment regimen and does not substitute for one. The RPR remained reactive at 1:16 on 2026-05-11 (R7d7a505d7a28). The patient is male and not pregnant. The episode is untreated.

No later signed correction by either record's author resolves the discrepancy, so the conflict is unresolved.

Late latent syphilis (Condition R0fa2dc5c6733); first benzathine penicillin dose 2024-08-12 (R2d42efddbddc). CDC 2021 recommends nontreponemal titers at 6, 12 and 24 months after treatment of latent syphilis. The 6-month test (due 2025-02-12, collected 2025-02-20, R70fefa59a83b) and the 12-month test (due 2025-08-12, collected 2025-08-14, R8511d5cd4d56) were both in window. The 24-month test was due 2026-08-12, window 2026-07-13 to 2026-09-11, which closed before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. The only candidate collection in that window is specimen Rd7a8a161a61b / result Ra1100072bf01 of 2026-08-05, whose collection label (GREENE, WALTER, MRN 74158126, DOB 1960-11-18) and accessioning entry (Basic R8afce1668a21: NGUYEN, THAO, MRN 40718826, DOB 1990-03-02) identify different patients, so the specimen's patient is unresolved. Whether a specimen from this patient was collected in the window therefore depends on an unresolved source conflict.

Secondary syphilis diagnosed 2025-11-04 (walk-in note R8c7e65f32e85: diffuse maculopapular rash of trunk, palms and soles, oral ulcer, RPR 1:64 reactive Rc1e01001897e, treponemal test reactive), more than 30 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. The only therapy given was azithromycin 2 g PO (R7649bfea645b). CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 recommend benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose for primary, secondary and early latent syphilis; azithromycin is not a recommended or alternative regimen for syphilis because of documented macrolide resistance in T. pallidum. Doxycycline 100 mg BID for 14 days would have been the acceptable alternative for a non-pregnant patient who refuses injection. No penicillin or doxycycline was ever given (follow-up note R7913a7ec16f8 documents continued refusal of injection and no alternative oral regimen), and the RPR remains reactive at 1:16 on 2026-05-12 (R63e65d051478). The patient is male and not pregnant. Treatment is inadequate for the infection.

Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-07-13 (Condition Ra97bed23c0ae; RPR 1:2 reactive, Radad9c2d8475), 73 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses (7.2 million units total) for late latent syphilis, and this is the regimen for pregnant as well as non-pregnant patients. Only dose 1 of 3 was given, on 2026-07-13 (Rab78b047578c, noted 'R gluteal. 1/3.'). Doses 2 and 3 were missed (no-shows 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-27, Rf9db26ead311 and R39055295d8e0) and the 2026-09-15 visit note (R650558441f29) states the series will be restarted once an hCG returns; no further doses are recorded. Treatment is inadequate on either pregnancy status.

Treatment for this late latent episode is incomplete (only 1 of 3 benzathine penicillin doses, Rab78b047578c), so if the patient was pregnant at any time from the 2026-07-13 diagnosis to the evaluation time the pregnancy issue would exist. Serum hCG was negative at diagnosis (R8cfaea610acb, 2026-07-13), but on 2026-09-15 she reported an LMP about 7 weeks earlier and a serum quantitative hCG was collected (R650558441f29). That specimen was collected before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time and has no final result: Observation R5dd8ded81561 is status registered with the laboratory comment 'In process.' Whether she was pregnant during the episode therefore turns on a pending test result.

Early latent syphilis (Condition R76b8fbdf9e4c) treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-07-07 (Rfaf358a1eb02). CDC 2021 recommends nontreponemal titers at 6, 12 and 24 months. The 6-month test was in window (due 2026-01-07, collected 2026-01-15, R08756c9095fb). The 12-month test was due 2026-07-07 with a window of 2026-06-07 to 2026-08-06, which closed before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time, and no specimen from this patient was collected in that window at this clinic. Under the local convention care at another facility is established only by a record from that facility received by the clinic, and no Maple Family Medicine record has been received, so whether a qualifying specimen was collected within the window cannot be determined.

Review request Rda4d87e0618a (third Bicillin dose 14 days after the second). Latent syphilis of unknown duration / late latent, diagnosed 2025-03-03 (Condition Rf59677b93814) in a patient who was pregnant at 18w3d that day (R2766ce143e8a). Doses were given 2025-03-03 (R94823194117b) and 2025-03-10 (R3730cec6d469); the third-week dose was missed for lack of transport (Rb9ddc85d5728) and given 2025-03-24 (R0678354279b3), 14 days after the second (R960530488cb5 confirms it was 'a week late'). CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 state that while an interval of 10-14 days between doses might be acceptable for non-pregnant patients, missed doses are not acceptable for pregnant patients receiving therapy for latent syphilis, and a pregnant patient who misses any dose must repeat the entire course. Given this patient's pregnancy status the interrupted series was not adequate therapy and no repeat course was given, so the issue is confirmed.

The patient was pregnant from before the 2025-03-03 diagnosis (18w3d, R2766ce143e8a) until delivery on 2025-08-01 (Riverside Hospital L&D discharge summary R362516686c03, a record from that facility received by the clinic). Treatment for latent syphilis of unknown duration in pregnancy requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses with no missed doses; CDC 2021 states that pregnant patients who miss any dose of therapy must repeat the full course. The third dose was given 2025-03-24, 14 days after the 2025-03-10 dose, because the 2025-03-17 dose was missed (Rb9ddc85d5728), and the course was never repeated. Treatment began 2025-03-03, which is more than 30 days before the 2025-08-01 delivery, so the timing requirement is met, but the regimen itself was not adequate for syphilis in pregnancy.

The name difference is explained by the registration update of 2026-01-12 (R2b6fca07ed75), which documents a legal name change from Maria Gomez to Maria Reyes with the MRN unchanged. Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-06-15 (Condition R8a5c5740c37c; RPR 1:16 with a nonreactive RPR 2025-11-20) in a patient with documented penicillin anaphylaxis (AllergyIntolerance R9e3c58cd24c2). She was dispensed and completed doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 14 days (MedicationDispense R351b92b15d48, 28 capsules; completion with no missed doses confirmed 2026-07-02, Ra2529680b361). Under CDC 2021 that is an acceptable alternative regimen for early syphilis in a non-pregnant, penicillin-allergic patient, but doxycycline is contraindicated in pregnancy: pregnant patients with syphilis must be treated with penicillin, desensitized if necessary. Pregnancy status is not established. The 2026-06-15 note (R43ca69f3d617) records an uncertain LMP with irregular cycles, and the serum quantitative hCG collected that day before the evaluation time has no final result (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, 'Specimen forwarded to reference laboratory'). Because adequacy depends on the patient's pregnancy status, which turns on that pending result, the issue cannot be determined.

The only syphilis therapy for this episode is doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days (MedicationDispense R351b92b15d48, completed per Ra2529680b361), which is not adequate treatment for syphilis in pregnancy; CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G, with penicillin desensitization for pregnant patients reporting penicillin allergy such as this patient's documented anaphylaxis (R9e3c58cd24c2). So the issue exists if and only if she was pregnant at some time between the 2026-06-15 diagnosis and the evaluation time. That fact is not established: the diagnosis-day note records an uncertain LMP with irregular cycles (R43ca69f3d617) and the serum quantitative hCG collected 2026-06-15, before the evaluation time, still has no final result (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, specimen forwarded to a reference laboratory). No delivery or other pregnancy record exists. The issue depends on a pending test result.

Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-05-19 (Condition Rbc8a9536c239; RPR 1:32, Rd403a1b46258), more than 30 days before the evaluation time. Adequate therapy is benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose. The administration record states that 2.4 million units IM were given on 2026-05-19 (MedicationAdministration R4e79a3b01676, status completed), but the pharmacy records conflict: only one 1,200,000-unit prefilled syringe was dispensed for him (MedicationDispense Rd6c2676fca98, quantity 1) and the pharmacist's signed end-of-day reconciliation states that one 1.2 MU syringe was released for this patient and that no second syringe was pulled from clinic stock for him per the cabinet log (DocumentReference R41e1cb337160). If only 1.2 million units were administered the dose is half the required amount. The two accounts are by different authors, so there is no later signed correction by a record's author to govern, and no other convention settles it; the administered dose is therefore an unresolved source conflict and adequacy cannot be determined.

Review request Re4a6b729e9c5 (was maternal treatment adequate for this delivery). Latent syphilis of unknown duration diagnosed 2025-09-15 (Condition Rb979a379e9e2; asymptomatic, last negative test unknown, RPR 1:8), more than 30 days before the evaluation time. Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-02-09 (Condition R06e8453cba94; RPR 1:32 reactive, Ra86dbdfb653a, with a nonreactive RPR in 10/2025 and reactive TP-PA), more than 30 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose (or, for a non-pregnant penicillin-allergic patient, doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days). No treatment was given: the visit note (R9a3fac1743ab) records that Bicillin was withheld on the reasoning that intermittent doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis had 'likely already partially treated' him, with a plan only to recheck the RPR. The only doxycycline in the chart is doxy-PEP, 20 tablets taken as 200 mg once within 72 hours after condomless sex (MedicationDispense R3496d34508d3 and refill R805872901be8), which is not a syphilis treatment regimen and does not substitute for one. The RPR remained reactive at 1:16 on 2026-05-11 (R7d7a505d7a28). The patient is male and not pregnant. The episode is untreated.

result.description: Review request R79d6d8df8dd9 (12-month RPR has no result on file). The 6-month test was in window (due 2026-02-18, collected 2026-02-24, R302c2679dbee). The 12-month test was due 2026-08-18, window 2026-07-19 to 2026-09-17. A serum specimen from this patient was collected 2026-09-14, inside that window: Specimen Raaaa95a95502 with label SCOTT, BRIANNA / MRN 55961553 / DOB 2001-03-17, matching the accessioning entry for accession A2609-2197 (Basic R0e0e55d93c73) and this patient's identifiers. Under the local convention a test is collected within its window when a specimen from the patient was collected then and not rejected, which is satisfied here, so follow-up is not overdue. The missing result is a pending result, not a missed collection.

Late latent syphilis (Condition R0fa2dc5c6733); first benzathine penicillin dose 2024-08-12 (R2d42efddbddc). The 6-month test (due 2025-02-12, collected 2025-02-20, R70fefa59a83b) and the 12-month test (due 2025-08-12, collected 2025-08-14, R8511d5cd4d56) were both in window. The only candidate collection in that window is specimen Rd7a8a161a61b / result Ra1100072bf01 of 2026-08-05, whose collection label (GREENE, WALTER, MRN 74158126, DOB 1960-11-18) and accessioning entry (Basic R8afce1668a21: NGUYEN, THAO, MRN 40718826, DOB 1990-03-02) identify different patients, so the specimen's patient is unresolved. Secondary syphilis diagnosed 2025-11-04 (walk-in note R8c7e65f32e85: diffuse maculopapular rash of trunk, palms and soles, oral ulcer, RPR 1:64 reactive Rc1e01001897e, treponemal test reactive), more than 30 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. The only therapy given was azithromycin 2 g PO (R7649bfea645b). CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 recommend benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose for primary, secondary and early latent syphilis; azithromycin is not a recommended or alternative regimen for syphilis because of documented macrolide resistance in T. pallidum. Doxycycline 100 mg BID for 14 days would have been the acceptable alternative for a non-pregnant patient who refuses injection. No penicillin or doxycycline was ever given (follow-up note R7913a7ec16f8 documents continued refusal of injection and no alternative oral regimen), and the RPR remains reactive at 1:16 on 2026-05-12 (R63e65d051478). The patient is male and not pregnant. Treatment is inadequate for the infection.

Only dose 1 of 3 was given, on 2026-07-13 (Rab78b047578c, noted 'R gluteal. 1/3.'). Doses 2 and 3 were missed (no-shows 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-27, Rf9db26ead311 and R39055295d8e0) and the 2026-09-15 visit note (R650558441f29) states the series will be restarted once an hCG returns; no further doses are recorded. Treatment is inadequate on either pregnancy status.

Treatment for this late latent episode is incomplete (only 1 of 3 benzathine penicillin doses, Rab78b047578c), so if the patient was pregnant at any time from the 2026-07-13 diagnosis to the evaluation time the pregnancy issue would exist. Serum hCG was negative at diagnosis (R8cfaea610acb, 2026-07-13), but on 2026-09-15 she reported an LMP about 7 weeks earlier and a serum quantitative hCG was collected (R650558441f29). That specimen was collected before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time and has no final result: Observation R5dd8ded81561 is status registered with the laboratory comment 'In process.' Whether she was pregnant during the episode therefore turns on a pending test result.

Early latent syphilis (Condition R76b8fbdf9e4c) treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-07-07 (Rfaf358a1eb02). Review request Rda4d87e0618a (third Bicillin dose 14 days after the second). Latent syphilis of unknown duration / late latent, diagnosed 2025-03-03 (Condition Rf59677b93814) in a patient who was pregnant at 18w3d that day (R2766ce143e8a). Doses were given 2025-03-03 (R94823194117b) and 2025-03-10 (R3730cec6d469); the third-week dose was missed for lack of transport (Rb9ddc85d5728) and given 2025-03-24 (R0678354279b3), 14 days after the second (R960530488cb5 confirms it was 'a week late'). CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 state that while an interval of 10-14 days between doses might be acceptable for non-pregnant patients, missed doses are not acceptable for pregnant patients receiving therapy for latent syphilis, and a pregnant patient who misses any dose must repeat the entire course. Given this patient's pregnancy status the interrupted series was not adequate therapy and no repeat course was given, so the issue is confirmed.

The patient was pregnant from before the 2025-03-03 diagnosis (18w3d, R2766ce143e8a) until delivery on 2025-08-01 (Riverside Hospital L&D discharge summary R362516686c03, a record from that facility received by the clinic). Treatment for latent syphilis of unknown duration in pregnancy requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses with no missed doses; CDC 2021 states that pregnant patients who miss any dose of therapy must repeat the full course. The third dose was given 2025-03-24, 14 days after the 2025-03-10 dose, because the 2025-03-17 dose was missed (Rb9ddc85d5728), and the course was never repeated. Treatment began 2025-03-03, which is more than 30 days before the 2025-08-01 delivery, so the timing requirement is met, but the regimen itself was not adequate for syphilis in pregnancy.

Review request R0db9ef904603 (only one of three Bicillin doses in our administration record). The test was collected within its window, so follow-up is not overdue.

Review request R798fc8df7ab4 (one Bicillin injection documented; is treatment complete). Syphilis diagnosed 2026-03-10, more than 30 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. The diagnostic note (R96a2514fb74d) records an asymptomatic new patient found on a pre-operative screen: RPR 1:16 (R0ead57315bb5) with reactive TP-PA (R42a74980be01), no sores, rash, alopecia, visual, hearing or neurologic findings, no known prior syphilis testing, and no documented negative test within the preceding year. With no evidence that infection was acquired within the past 12 months, this is latent syphilis of unknown duration, which CDC 2021 directs be treated as late latent: benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses. Only a single dose was given, on 2026-03-10 (R86fd16f52ecf, 1.2 MU in each ventrogluteal site for 2.4 MU total), and the 2026-03-24 call note (R9df69739138f) records that no further appointments were scheduled. Serum hCG was negative (R7d1db2470e17) and nothing indicates pregnancy, so the required regimen is three weekly doses. Two doses are missing; treatment is inadequate.

Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2025-06-02 (Condition R7a35247e4cfc) requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses. Doses were given 2025-06-02 (R28fb18460ef4) and 2025-06-09 (Radd0c0084f66), but the 2025-06-16 dose was cancelled for out-of-state travel (Rda877498a8cf) and the third dose was not given until 2025-06-27 (R49231f4025c9), 18 days after the second. CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 note that for non-pregnant patients an interval of 10-14 days between doses of benzathine penicillin might be acceptable before restarting the sequence of injections; an 18-day interval exceeds that allowance, so the sequence should have been restarted. No restarted course is recorded (R84aa6677a1c5 simply declares the series complete). The patient is male and not pregnant. Treatment as given is not adequate for late latent syphilis.

No treatment was given: the visit note (R9a3fac1743ab) records that Bicillin was withheld on the reasoning that intermittent doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis had 'likely already partially treated' him, with a plan only to recheck the RPR. The only doxycycline in the chart is doxy-PEP, 20 tablets taken as 200 mg once within 72 hours after condomless sex (MedicationDispense R3496d34508d3 and refill R805872901be8), which is not a syphilis treatment regimen and does not substitute for one. The RPR remained reactive at 1:16 on 2026-05-11 (R7d7a505d7a28). The patient is male and not pregnant. The episode is untreated.

Review request R79d6d8df8dd9 (12-month RPR has no result on file). Primary syphilis (Condition R8221b078a309) treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-08-18 (Rdbe347ecbfcf); CDC 2021 recommends nontreponemal titers at 6 and 12 months. The 6-month test was in window (due 2026-02-18, collected 2026-02-24, R302c2679dbee). The 12-month test was due 2026-08-18, window 2026-07-19 to 2026-09-17. A serum specimen from this patient was collected 2026-09-14, inside that window: Specimen Raaaa95a95502 with label SCOTT, BRIANNA / MRN 55961553 / DOB 2001-03-17, matching the accessioning entry for accession A2609-2197 (Basic R0e0e55d93c73) and this patient's identifiers. The laboratory did not reject it; the comment on Observation R1e1c26c47f5d (status registered) is 'Received at reference laboratory. Result to follow.' Under the local convention a test is collected within its window when a specimen from the patient was collected then and not rejected, which is satisfied here, so follow-up is not overdue. The missing result is a pending result, not a missed collection.

Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-01-20 (Condition R049a64ea2ca4) requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses. Only dose 1 of 3 is recorded here, on 2026-01-20 (MedicationAdministration R7190edc51f1a, 'R gluteal. #1 of 3.'). On 2026-01-29 the patient reported that she had moved to Riverton, had received her second Bicillin injection at Eastside Community Health on 2026-01-27, and had the third scheduled there for 2026-02-03; a release of information was signed and faxed (R496b28b30760), and a second request was faxed on 2026-03-02 with no response to the first (R5c674c520644). Under the local convention care at another facility is established only by a record from that facility received by the clinic, and no Eastside Community Health administration record has been received. Whether doses 2 and 3 were given, and so whether treatment is adequate, depends on that outstanding outside record. Serology is consistent with either possibility (RPR 1:1 on 2026-07-22, R53468b9b4173).

before.description: Review request R7922bcafda1e (8/5 RPR identification discrepancy). The 2026-08-05 quantitative RPR (Ra1100072bf01, Nonreactive) filed in this episode's chart is linked to specimen Rd7a8a161a61b, whose collection label reads GREENE, WALTER / MRN 74158126 / DOB 1960-11-18 (matching this patient), while the laboratory accessioning entry for the same accession A2608-2838 (Basic R8afce1668a21) reads NGUYEN, THAO / MRN 40718826 / DOB 1990-03-02. Under the local convention a specimen and its result belong to the patient identified by MRN and DOB on both the collection record and the accessioning entry; because these identify different patients the specimen's patient is unresolved, so whether this result belongs to a different patient cannot be determined. No later signed correction by either record's author resolves the discrepancy, so the conflict is unresolved.

Late latent syphilis (Condition R0fa2dc5c6733); first benzathine penicillin dose 2024-08-12 (R2d42efddbddc). CDC 2021 recommends nontreponemal titers at 6, 12 and 24 months after treatment of latent syphilis. The 6-month test (due 2025-02-12, collected 2025-02-20, R70fefa59a83b) and the 12-month test (due 2025-08-12, collected 2025-08-14, R8511d5cd4d56) were both in window. The 24-month test was due 2026-08-12, window 2026-07-13 to 2026-09-11, which closed before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. The only candidate collection in that window is specimen Rd7a8a161a61b / result Ra1100072bf01 of 2026-08-05, whose collection label (GREENE, WALTER, MRN 74158126, DOB 1960-11-18) and accessioning entry (Basic R8afce1668a21: NGUYEN, THAO, MRN 40718826, DOB 1990-03-02) identify different patients, so the specimen's patient is unresolved. Whether a specimen from this patient was collected in the window therefore depends on an unresolved source conflict.

Secondary syphilis diagnosed 2025-11-04 (walk-in note R8c7e65f32e85: diffuse maculopapular rash of trunk, palms and soles, oral ulcer, RPR 1:64 reactive Rc1e01001897e, treponemal test reactive), more than 30 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. The only therapy given was azithromycin 2 g PO (R7649bfea645b). CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 recommend benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose for primary, secondary and early latent syphilis; azithromycin is not a recommended or alternative regimen for syphilis because of documented macrolide resistance in T. pallidum. Doxycycline 100 mg BID for 14 days would have been the acceptable alternative for a non-pregnant patient who refuses injection. No penicillin or doxycycline was ever given (follow-up note R7913a7ec16f8 documents continued refusal of injection and no alternative oral regimen), and the RPR remains reactive at 1:16 on 2026-05-12 (R63e65d051478). The patient is male and not pregnant. Treatment is inadequate for the infection.

Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-07-13 (Condition Ra97bed23c0ae; RPR 1:2 reactive, Radad9c2d8475), 73 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses (7.2 million units total) for late latent syphilis, and this is the regimen for pregnant as well as non-pregnant patients. Only dose 1 of 3 was given, on 2026-07-13 (Rab78b047578c, noted 'R gluteal. 1/3.'). Doses 2 and 3 were missed (no-shows 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-27, Rf9db26ead311 and R39055295d8e0) and the 2026-09-15 visit note (R650558441f29) states the series will be restarted once an hCG returns; no further doses are recorded. Treatment is inadequate on either pregnancy status.

Treatment for this late latent episode is incomplete (only 1 of 3 benzathine penicillin doses, Rab78b047578c), so if the patient was pregnant at any time from the 2026-07-13 diagnosis to the evaluation time the pregnancy issue would exist. Serum hCG was negative at diagnosis (R8cfaea610acb, 2026-07-13), but on 2026-09-15 she reported an LMP about 7 weeks earlier and a serum quantitative hCG was collected (R650558441f29). That specimen was collected before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time and has no final result: Observation R5dd8ded81561 is status registered with the laboratory comment 'In process.' Whether she was pregnant during the episode therefore turns on a pending test result.

Early latent syphilis (Condition R76b8fbdf9e4c) treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-07-07 (Rfaf358a1eb02). CDC 2021 recommends nontreponemal titers at 6, 12 and 24 months. The 6-month test was in window (due 2026-01-07, collected 2026-01-15, R08756c9095fb). The 12-month test was due 2026-07-07 with a window of 2026-06-07 to 2026-08-06, which closed before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time, and no specimen from this patient was collected in that window at this clinic. The 2026-08-12 outreach note (Ra01873897ab4) records the patient stating she had 'the syphilis blood test' in July at her PCP, Dr. Lin at Maple Family Medicine, and that a request was faxed for the result. Under the local convention care at another facility is established only by a record from that facility received by the clinic, and no Maple Family Medicine record has been received, so whether a qualifying specimen was collected within the window cannot be determined.

Review request Rda4d87e0618a (third Bicillin dose 14 days after the second). Latent syphilis of unknown duration / late latent, diagnosed 2025-03-03 (Condition Rf59677b93814) in a patient who was pregnant at 18w3d that day (R2766ce143e8a). Doses were given 2025-03-03 (R94823194117b) and 2025-03-10 (R3730cec6d469); the third-week dose was missed for lack of transport (Rb9ddc85d5728) and given 2025-03-24 (R0678354279b3), 14 days after the second (R960530488cb5 confirms it was 'a week late'). CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 state that while an interval of 10-14 days between doses might be acceptable for non-pregnant patients, missed doses are not acceptable for pregnant patients receiving therapy for latent syphilis, and a pregnant patient who misses any dose must repeat the entire course. Given this patient's pregnancy status the interrupted series was not adequate therapy and no repeat course was given, so the issue is confirmed.

The patient was pregnant from before the 2025-03-03 diagnosis (18w3d, R2766ce143e8a) until delivery on 2025-08-01 (Riverside Hospital L&D discharge summary R362516686c03, a record from that facility received by the clinic). Treatment for latent syphilis of unknown duration in pregnancy requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses with no missed doses; CDC 2021 states that pregnant patients who miss any dose of therapy must repeat the full course. The third dose was given 2025-03-24, 14 days after the 2025-03-10 dose, because the 2025-03-17 dose was missed (Rb9ddc85d5728), and the course was never repeated. Treatment began 2025-03-03, which is more than 30 days before the 2025-08-01 delivery, so the timing requirement is met, but the regimen itself was not adequate for syphilis in pregnancy.

The 2026-06-16 quantitative RPR (Observation R29b26b182ad8, Nonreactive) is filed with this patient as subject, but its specimen collection record (Specimen R4c90adf34f8e, accession A2606-2157) carries label name ORTIZ, SAMANTHA with MRN 48305482 and DOB 1998-08-13, and the laboratory accessioning entry for the same accession (Basic R1e96d0922c32) also reads ORTIZ, SAMANTHA / 48305482 / 1998-08-13. Samuel Ortega is MRN 24530063, DOB 1983-01-26. Because the collection record and the accessioning entry agree and both identify Samantha Ortiz (Patient P86f7f3d), the specimen and its result belong to her, not to this patient. A laboratory result belonging to a different patient is filed in this episode's chart.

The 12-month test was due 2026-06-09 with a window of 2026-05-10 to 2026-07-09, which closed before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. No specimen from Samuel Ortega was collected in the window, and no outreach or outside record suggests otherwise, so the 12-month follow-up test was not collected within its window.

Primary syphilis diagnosed 2026-04-20 (Condition Re1cac7dd6145; indurated painless chancre, RPR 1:16 reactive Re4bdecc928e7, treponemal test reactive), more than 30 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose. The ordered injection was never given: MedicationAdministration Rab08552226b7 has status not-done with the note 'Pt left the clinic before the injection was given.' Outreach failed (R8f41005f28cc) and a DIS referral was placed for untreated primary syphilis (R7db676cad2c0). No other treatment of any kind is recorded, and the patient is male and not pregnant, so the episode remains untreated.

Review request R0db9ef904603 (only one of three Bicillin doses in our administration record). Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2025-04-14 (Condition Rde97ef6f5e9c) requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses. Dose 1 was given here on 2025-04-14 (R08ad4910274b). Because weekly travel was impossible, doses 2 and 3 were transferred to the County Health Department STD Clinic with a signed release (R3236bca81c51), and the clinic has received that facility's own faxed medication administration record (DocumentReference Rf4b6f607dc06, author County Health Department STD Clinic), documenting Bicillin L-A 2.4 MU IM on 2025-04-21 and 2025-04-28 and stating the series is complete 3 of 3. The outside care is therefore established by a record from that facility received by the clinic, and the three doses fall at 7-day intervals. Treatment is adequate for late latent syphilis in a non-pregnant male; the gap is only in the clinic's internal MAR.

Review request R9742468728aa (no 12-month RPR result in this chart). Early latent syphilis (Condition R312b4315e4e1) treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-06-23 (R358faf9cf732); titers are due at 6, 12 and 24 months. The 6-month test was in window (due 2025-12-23, collected 2025-12-29, R0279bed8a8ae). The 12-month test was due 2026-06-23, window 2026-05-24 to 2026-07-23. A specimen from this patient was collected on 2026-06-16 within that window: Specimen R4c90adf34f8e, label ORTIZ, SAMANTHA / MRN 48305482 / DOB 1998-08-13, matching this patient, and the laboratory accessioning entry for the same accession A2606-2157 (Basic R1e96d0922c32) carries the identical identifiers, so the specimen is hers. The nursing note of 2026-06-16 (R1f9eae76e46b) documents the 12-month draw. The specimen was not rejected and was resulted as Nonreactive; the result was simply filed in Samuel Ortega's chart (Observation R29b26b182ad8), which is a misfiling in that chart rather than a missed collection here. The test was collected within its window, so follow-up is not overdue.

Early latent syphilis (Condition Ree07a4fa48b4) treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM on 2025-02-24 (R76a7ae364846). CDC 2021 recommends nontreponemal titers at 6, 12 and 24 months. The 6-month test was in window (due 2025-08-24, collected 2025-09-02, Ra66fa8daaa9c). The 12-month test was due 2026-02-24 with a window of 2026-01-25 to 2026-03-26, which closed before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. No specimen from this patient was collected in that window; the chart contains only failed outreach (2026-02-10 calls, number not in service, letter sent, R0d07949b4f34; 2026-03-20 letter returned undeliverable, R34c296c82dae) and no indication of testing at any other facility. The 12-month follow-up test was not collected within its window.

Review request R798fc8df7ab4 (one Bicillin injection documented; is treatment complete). Syphilis diagnosed 2026-03-10, more than 30 days before the 2026-09-24 evaluation time. The diagnostic note (R96a2514fb74d) records an asymptomatic new patient found on a pre-operative screen: RPR 1:16 (R0ead57315bb5) with reactive TP-PA (R42a74980be01), no sores, rash, alopecia, visual, hearing or neurologic findings, no known prior syphilis testing, and no documented negative test within the preceding year. With no evidence that infection was acquired within the past 12 months, this is latent syphilis of unknown duration, which CDC 2021 directs be treated as late latent: benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses. Only a single dose was given, on 2026-03-10 (R86fd16f52ecf, 1.2 MU in each ventrogluteal site for 2.4 MU total), and the 2026-03-24 call note (R9df69739138f) records that no further appointments were scheduled. Serum hCG was negative (R7d1db2470e17) and nothing indicates pregnancy, so the required regimen is three weekly doses. Two doses are missing; treatment is inadequate.

Late latent syphilis diagnosed 2025-06-02 (Condition R7a35247e4cfc) requires benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses. Doses were given 2025-06-02 (R28fb18460ef4) and 2025-06-09 (Radd0c0084f66), but the 2025-06-16 dose was cancelled for out-of-state travel (Rda877498a8cf) and the third dose was not given until 2025-06-27 (R49231f4025c9), 18 days after the second. CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, 2021 note that for non-pregnant patients an interval of 10-14 days between doses of benzathine penicillin might be acceptable before restarting the sequence of injections; an 18-day interval exceeds that allowance, so the sequence should have been restarted. No restarted course is recorded (R84aa6677a1c5 simply declares the series complete). The patient is male and not pregnant. Treatment as given is not adequate for late latent syphilis.

Review request R0d7a56e007e3 (specimen label name does not match the current chart name for the 4/8 RPR). The 2026-04-08 quantitative RPR (Observation Rc7f2214aaf95, Reactive 1:4) rests on specimen R2e18a9ea8714, whose label reads GOMEZ, MARIA with MRN 53229432 and DOB 1989-04-02, and the laboratory accessioning entry for the same accession A2604-6204 (Basic Re7b5f29d83cd) reads GOMEZ, MARIA / 53229432 / 1989-04-02. Under the local convention the specimen and its result belong to the patient identified by medical record number and date of birth on the collection record and on the accessioning entry; both carry this patient's MRN 53229432 and DOB 1989-04-02, and they agree with each other, so the specimen is hers. The name difference is explained by the registration update of 2026-01-12 (R2b6fca07ed75), which documents a legal name change from Maria Gomez to Maria Reyes with the MRN unchanged. The result does not belong to a different patient.

Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-06-15 (Condition R8a5c5740c37c; RPR 1:16 with a nonreactive RPR 2025-11-20) in a patient with documented penicillin anaphylaxis (AllergyIntolerance R9e3c58cd24c2). She was dispensed and completed doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 14 days (MedicationDispense R351b92b15d48, 28 capsules; completion with no missed doses confirmed 2026-07-02, Ra2529680b361). Under CDC 2021 that is an acceptable alternative regimen for early syphilis in a non-pregnant, penicillin-allergic patient, but doxycycline is contraindicated in pregnancy: pregnant patients with syphilis must be treated with penicillin, desensitized if necessary. Pregnancy status is not established. The 2026-06-15 note (R43ca69f3d617) records an uncertain LMP with irregular cycles, and the serum quantitative hCG collected that day before the evaluation time has no final result (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, 'Specimen forwarded to reference laboratory'). Because adequacy depends on the patient's pregnancy status, which turns on that pending result, the issue cannot be determined.

The only syphilis therapy for this episode is doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days (MedicationDispense R351b92b15d48, completed per Ra2529680b361), which is not adequate treatment for syphilis in pregnancy; CDC 2021 requires benzathine penicillin G, with penicillin desensitization for pregnant patients reporting penicillin allergy such as this patient's documented anaphylaxis (R9e3c58cd24c2). So the issue exists if and only if she was pregnant at some time between the 2026-06-15 diagnosis and the evaluation time. That fact is not established: the diagnosis-day note records an uncertain LMP with irregular cycles (R43ca69f3d617) and the serum quantitative hCG collected 2026-06-15, before the evaluation time, still has no final result (Observation R49f81c509bab, status registered, specimen forwarded to a reference laboratory). No delivery or other pregnancy record exists. The issue depends on a pending test result.

Early latent syphilis diagnosed 2026-05-19 (Condition Rbc8a9536c239; RPR 1:32, Rd403a1b46258), more than 30 days before the evaluation time. Adequate therapy is benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM in a single dose. The administration record states that 2.4 million units IM were given on 2026-05-19 (MedicationAdministration R4e79a3b01676, status completed), but the pharmacy records conflict: only one 1,200,000-unit prefilled syringe was dispensed for him (MedicationDispense Rd6c2676fca98, quantity 1) and the pharmacist's signed end-of-day reconciliation states that one 1.2 MU syringe was released for this patient and that no second syringe was pulled from clinic stock for him per the cabinet log (DocumentReference R41e1cb337160). If only 1.2 million units were administered the dose is half the required amount. The two accounts are by different authors, so there is no later signed correction by a record's author to govern, and no other convention settles it; the administered dose is therefore an unresolved source conflict and adequacy cannot be determined.

Review request Re4a6b729e9c5 (was maternal treatment adequate for this delivery). The patient was pregnant from the 2026-01-05 diagnosis, presenting at 35w1d with latent syphilis of unknown duration (Rabd804816606, Condition R35a03bed1367). She received the correct regimen, benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses, on 2026-01-05, 2026-01-12 and 2026-01-19 at exactly 7-day intervals (Rc541e07b1a97, R0083a427d4e3, Reb8ecf233de2; series completion confirmed at 38w1d, Reef7fc18efd3). However, once delivery has occurred that treatment must have begun at least 30 days before it, and treatment began 2026-01-05, so 2026-02-04 is the decisive date. The delivery date is not established: the only record of it is the 2026-02-20 telephone note in which the patient reports having delivered at Mercy General, with maternal delivery records and the newborn discharge summary requested from Mercy General (R2f4e5f4a8666). At 35w1d on 2026-01-05 her estimated due date was about 2026-02-08, so delivery could have fallen on either side of 2026-02-04. Care at another facility is established only by a record from that facility received by the clinic, and no Mercy General record has been received, so the issue cannot be determined.

Latent syphilis of unknown duration diagnosed 2025-09-15 (Condition Rb979a379e9e2; asymptomatic, last negative test unknown, RPR 1:8), more than 30 days before the evaluation time. CDC 2021 directs that latent syphilis of unknown duration be treated as late latent with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for 3 doses, and the plan was documented as weekly x3 with return visits 9/22 and 9/29 (R9314a09ccd1b). Only the first dose was given, on 2025-09-15 (R302e2c011a98). The patient did not attend for doses 2 or 3 (no-shows documented 2025-09-22 and 2025-09-29 with voicemails and a mailed letter, R5bb174ddeeae and R7ce2618288da) and no further doses appear anywhere in the chart; the RPR remained reactive at 1:4 on 2026-03-20 (R289dfecbca57). The patient is male and not pregnant. Treatment is inadequate.
